hypothesis: Question: does the level relationship between a 2012 hour and the same hour one year (52 weeks, weekday-aligned) earlier transfer into the later period better than (a) letting trees infer level from yr/elapsed_day alone or (b) a global exponential trend? Prior evidence changed my view: idea-816bb1 fitted a global log-linear trend (annual factor 2.16 on train-only daily totals) and deflated/re-inflated targets; it degraded development RMSE to 81.03 vs 59.98 for the fixed-HGB leader idea-ae78bf (which itself matched baseline-2 at 59.99, so target-transform branches added nothing). This suggests a global multiplicative growth extrapolation overshoots, while trees using yr already carry most of the transferable level. Instead of extrapolating a trend, this program supplies a local anchor: for each row, the training-label rental count at elapsed_day-364 with the same hr ('lag_point'), and a smoothed version averaging the same hour at lag 357/364/371 plus the mean daily total over the week around lag 364 ('lag_smooth'), both alongside the original covariates; missing values (all 2011 rows) are left NaN for HGB. Branches base/lag_point/lag_smooth use identical fixed baseline HGB hyperparameters and are selected by mean RMSE over two forward 61-day training holdouts exactly as in idea-ae78bf, so the only changed factor per branch is the feature set. Contrasting expectations: if the previous-year hourly relationship transfers, lag_smooth should beat base in fold 1 (holdout Mar-Apr 2012, the only fold where training rows carry lags) and development RMSE should fall below ~57 (>=5% relative gain) without equal-date MAE worsening; if the lag columns act mainly as a yr proxy confounded with missingness, or previous-year weather noise dominates, the gain will be nil (~60) or negative, which would be an informative negative about year-over-year hourly transfer. Fold 2 (holdout Jan-Feb 2012) cannot learn lag relationships because all its training rows are 2011; this is reported rather than hidden. The program also reports train-only year-over-year monthly daily-total ratios for Jan-Apr 2012 vs 2011 to check the 2.16 annual factor assumed by idea-816bb1. Program-authored findings are diagnostics on training data only, not evaluation-label metrics.
